name: Spatial Freq Temporal
algorithm: Spatial Freq Temporal — Frequency Domain Analyzer
mechanism:
This method analyzes the temporal behavior of spatial frequency content across video frames for deepfake detection:

1. **Per-Frame Spatial Frequency Decomposition**: Each frame is decomposed into spatial frequency bands via 2D FFT or wavelet transform. The energy at each spatial frequency is tracked over time, creating a 3D representation (spatial frequency × orientation × time).

2. **Frequency Stability Analysis**: For static regions, the spatial frequency content should remain stable across frames. The method measures temporal variance at each spatial frequency. Deepfake generation may produce temporally varying frequency content — particularly at high frequencies where generation artifacts fluctuate frame-to-frame.

3. **Face-Background Frequency Coherence**: The temporal behavior of spatial frequencies in face regions vs. background should be similar (same imaging pipeline). The method compares temporal frequency stability between regions. Different temporal stability characteristics indicate different generation/capture sources.

4. **Spectral Flicker Detection**: The method detects temporal oscillations in specific spatial frequency bands. These "spectral flickers" can arise from: (a) GAN training instabilities producing oscillating artifacts, (b) autoencoder quantization varying between frames, (c) frame-rate conversion creating frequency-domain beating patterns.

5. **Natural Image Statistics Temporal Consistency**: Natural images follow the 1/f spatial frequency power spectrum (scale invariance). This relationship should hold consistently across frames. The method tracks the spectral slope over time — systematic temporal variations in the 1/f exponent indicate processing artifacts from AI generation.
parameters:
Analysis type: frequency
Media: video
Input: Video frames extracted at key intervals
Output: Confidence score (0-100)
Frame sampling: Adaptive (1-5 fps depending on method)
Temporal window: Sliding window across frame sequence
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-88% standalone accuracy. Most effective when combined with other video forensic methods. Performance depends on video quality, resolution, and compression level.
source: Video forensics and deepfake detection research. Based on computer vision and temporal signal analysis methods.
useCase: Detection of deepfake and AI-generated video through spatial freq temporal analysis. This method examines temporal and spatial features that are difficult for AI systems to perfectly replicate, providing evidence for video authenticity assessment.
strengths:
• Captures temporal artifacts that single-frame analysis misses
• Works with standard video formats
• Effective against common deepfake techniques
• Can be combined with other video forensic methods
• Based on established computer vision research
limitations:
• Performance affected by video compression and resolution
• Some methods require sufficient frame count for temporal analysis
• Effectiveness varies with deepfake generation technique
• Best used as part of a comprehensive multi-method pipeline
• May produce false positives on heavily edited authentic video
